note: No. 58. The printed name, "Jerzego a raczej Bogusława Gerke", is struck out in pen, and the messenger wrote a name in the left margin with marks to show where it goes: "Marcina" and a surname. The scribble below them is his paraph (his flourish), not a third word. I read the surname as Hetke, with doubt. The first button is what the text has now.

note: No. 7, "Jana Fryderyka Rasch". The printed second name is covered by pen strokes. Is it struck out (so the man is Jan Rasch), or did the messenger write another name over it? If another name, type it under "Something else".
No. 55, "Henryka Celmer". The first letter is written over in pen and looks like a Z. The print has Celmer for all the family; the English gives Zelmer either way.

Nos. 53 and 54, "Pawła Rogackiego" and "Stanisława Rogackiego" (the same picture as the row above). In both the messenger wrote a c over a printed letter. I read the first letter of the print as R, so both are Rogackiego; your earlier text had Bogackiego for no. 53.
No. 70, "Krystjana Grünwald": the name breaks across two lines ("Kry-" / "stjana"), and on the second line the letters "ja" are written over in pen. What do they read now?

Page 4, under the print at the left: "Koszta" (costs) and "Raz Rs .. k 21." (in all, silver roubles and 21 kopecks), beside the messenger's signature. The figure of roubles is blotted; I read 47. If it is right, it is the cost of serving all 97 copies.
